fatal_errors: The proposed method is DFT-based composition and structure screening, whereas the demonstrated tuning methods were 700 K annealing, elastic tensile strain, and control of nanoribbon spacing.
DFT is presented as directly tuning the material, although it is a predictive tool rather than the physical intervention studied.
The assumed disordered FCC structure conflicts with the amorphous or extremely fine disordered state having only cubic-type short-range order.
The asserted 250–350 K range, 300 K entropy-change values, 20% enhancement, and composition bounds are unsupported and inconsistent with the reported broad 40–200 K response and peak near 140 K.

The hypothesis omits the central mechanism: short-range atomic reordering and internal-strain relaxation without crystallization, together with magnetoelastic coupling and geometry-dependent inter-ribbon coupling.
No supporting evidence is cited for the quantitative predictions.
explanation: The response identifies the broad goal of tuning magnetocaloric HEAs and proposes a test involving magnetization and entropy-change measurements, but it does not reconstruct the study. The relevant method was controlled post-fabrication processing and geometry: annealing at 700 K enhanced magnetic alignment and entropy change through short-range relaxation without bulk crystallization; elastic strain altered the higher-temperature response through magnetoelastic coupling; and increased ribbon spacing suppressed inter-ribbon coupling. The DFT proposal could be a generic alloy-screening strategy, but its structural assumptions, conditions, numerical outcomes, and baseline are invented. Its falsification experiment is only partly discriminating because failure of one predicted composition at 300 K would not establish that DFT is generally ineffective.
